memory_update.text: Core direct AI networking candidates for this node: NVDA, AVGO, ANET, MRVL, CRDO, ALAB, CSCO.
Core optical interconnect candidates for this node: COHR, LITE, FN, AAOI, CIEN; evidence should separate datacom AI demand from telecom and consumer optical cycles.
Second-order test and validation candidates: KEYS and VIAV; relevance depends on exposure to 800G/1.6T Ethernet, optical module validation, SerDes testing, and AI data-center buildouts.

The node should be tracked in sub-buckets: switching ASICs, complete Ethernet/InfiniBand systems, NICs/DPUs, optical transceivers, lasers/components, DSP/SerDes chips, active electrical cables, contract manufacturing, and network test/monitoring.

Many important optical module suppliers and silicon photonics players are Asia-listed or private; the US-listed universe may miss suppliers such as leading China/Taiwan optical module vendors and private silicon photonics startups.
Need market-cap verification for AAOI before dashboard promotion; included as a below-$1B exception because optical transceiver relevance is direct but financial and liquidity risks may be higher.

Falsification plan: downgrade the node if hyperscalers report adequate network supply, if AI cluster scaling bottlenecks shift mainly to power/cooling or GPU supply, if Ethernet commoditization compresses margins faster than volume growth, or if optical module supply becomes oversupplied.

node: AI networking, switches, NICs, optical modules, DSPs, and silicon photonics
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the AI networking and optical interconnect supply-chain node. The strongest direct mappings are Ethernet/InfiniBand switch and NIC vendors, merchant switching-silicon suppliers, optical transceiver/component suppliers, high-speed connectivity semiconductor vendors, contract manufacturers for optical modules, and test/measurement vendors used to validate high-speed networks. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell list. Several candidates are direct chokepoint candidates; others are second-order enablers or demand-side/cloud-network beneficiaries that require follow-up evidence on AI-specific revenue exposure.
